newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks slip at close on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks slip at close on Greenspan.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed with losses on Wednesday after comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan appeared to dealers to be a sign of forthcoming U.S. interest rate hikes.
The comments triggered sales across nearly all sectors.
The general index fell 1.65 points, 0.35 percent, to 465.76 and the Ibex-35 lost 22.56 points, 0.42 percent, to 5,311.36.
The bourse had been gaining ground up until Greenspan addressed the U.S. Senate, it then shifted sharply, to close at levels considered to be supports.
"The market responded to Greenspan's words, but it hasn't seen an avalanche of selling and the close isn't too bad," a portfolio manager said.
Trading volume was a bit more than 65 billion pesetas, similiar to the levels of recent days.
Repsol fell 20 pesetas to 5,560, after the industry ministry was reported as naming April/May for the sale of the state's remaining 10 percent stake in the energy group.
Banks were hit, with Argentaria and Popular losing the most with a 1.3 percent drop.
